intro: You're looking for a British citizenship advisor near you because you've decided to apply to naturalise or register as a British citizen, or you're helping someone who is. You want someone local who can check your residence and good character requirements, and guide you through the application and ceremony. We can introduce you to a suitably regulated immigration adviser near you who will quote you directly, with fees on application.
need_heading: What people searching for a British citizenship advisor near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want clear, local help to apply for naturalisation or registration without missing a detail that could delay or spoil the application.
needs: You have lived in the UK for the required time and want to check that your absences from the UK are within the allowed limits before you apply.
You are unsure whether something in your past could affect the good character assessment and want advice on how to present your case.
You need help completing the application form and gathering the right documents, such as evidence of residence and your English language or life in the UK test.
You have a more complex situation, perhaps because you were born outside the UK to British parents or you are applying to register a child as British.
You have received a decision and want to understand what happens next, including booking and attending your citizenship ceremony.
context_heading: What to understand before you choose an adviser
context: It is a criminal offence to give immigration advice in the UK unless the adviser is qualified and regulated. Advisers must be registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA, formerly the OISC) at the right level for your matter, or be a solicitor, barrister or chartered legal executive authorised by their own regulator. You can check the IAA's adviser finder or the Solicitors Regulation Authority register before you share documents or pay anyone.

IAA advisers are registered at levels that limit what they can do, from basic applications to appeals and representation. Ask what level an adviser holds and whether it covers your type of case. iComply is not regulated and does not give advice; we simply introduce you to a professional who can.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say that you are looking for a British citizenship advisor near you, and give your postcode or the area you would like the adviser to cover.
Explain whether you are applying for naturalisation or for registration as a British citizen, and whether the application is for yourself or for someone else, such as a child.
Mention any concerns about absences from the UK or about the good character requirement, so we can introduce you to someone used to handling similar points.
Let us know if you have already started an application or received any correspondence from the Home Office.
Tell us about any particular communication needs or accessibility requirements you have for meetings.
Confirm that you understand the adviser will quote you directly and that fees are on application.
questions: Are you registered with the Immigration Advice Authority, and at what level?
If you are a solicitor, barrister or chartered legal executive, which regulator authorises you?
Have you handled British citizenship applications like mine before?
How will you check that my absences from the UK are within the limits?
What evidence will you need from me about good character, and how will you assess it?
What are your fees and what do they cover, including any disbursements?

faqs.q: Do I need a British citizenship advisor near me, or can I apply myself?
faqs.a: You can apply yourself, but an adviser can help you check residence and good character requirements and avoid common mistakes. If your case is straightforward you may feel confident to apply directly, but if you have any doubts, advice can be worthwhile.

faqs.q: How do I check that an adviser is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Use the Immigration Advice Authority's adviser finder to check registration and level, or the Solicitors Regulation Authority register if they are a solicitor. Never share documents or pay anyone until you have checked.

faqs.q: What does 'price on application' mean for iComply's service?
faqs.a: It means the professional you are introduced to will quote you directly for the work you need. iComply does not set fees; you will receive a clear quote from the adviser before any work begins.

faqs.q: What happens after my citizenship application is approved?
faqs.a: If your application is approved, you will usually need to attend a citizenship ceremony and take an oath or affirmation of allegiance. Your adviser can explain what to expect and help you prepare.
